header.name: Dairy_V3
header.full_name: Dairy plant V3: cheese and biogas from whey
header.authors_and_contributors: Sophia Wallerand, Daniel Flórez-Orrego, Pullah Bhatnagar, Oktay Boztas, Dareen Dardor, EPFL IPESE research group
header.description: Cheese dairy whose whey and wastewater sludge are digested into biogas and fertiliser, with the options to burn the biogas in a cogeneration engine or to upgrade it to biomethane. 27 thermal streams per 1 t/h of fresh milk.

units.unit_description: This unit processes 1 t/h of fresh milk into cream and cheese: reception, pasteurisation with regenerative heat exchange and cream separation, three-effect evaporation of the skimmed milk, cheese making and brining, cleaning in place and wastewater treatment. The whey and the sludge of the wastewater treatment are digested at 55 °C into biogas with 55 vol % methane; the digestate is dried with steam into a liquid fertiliser and a dried digestate. In the OSMOSE model, the heat streams are grouped by section into the units Pasteurisation, Evaporation, Cheese, CIP and Biogas, and the material flows and the electricity into the unit Plant_boundary, all at the scale CAPACITY.
units.connectors_description: The unit takes fresh milk, salt, water for brining and water for cleaning (CIP), and electricity, and delivers cream, cheese, biogas (55 vol % CH4), liquid fertiliser, dried digestate, digester wastewater, evaporator condensate water, treated water discharge and CIP water discharge. The material flows close at 1,187.3 kg/h in and out.

units.heat_streams_description: 13 cold and 14 hot streams per 1 t/h of fresh milk, from the dairy model of Dardor et al. (2024). The evaporator is described effect by effect. Phase changes at constant temperature have a span of 0.1 K; the ΔTmin/2 contribution is 5 K for liquid streams and 2 K for boiling and condensing streams; the digestate dryer (C13, H13) keeps the 2.5 K of the source model. Streams ending below about 20 °C need refrigeration unless another process stream absorbs their heat.

units.unit_description: Option for the use of the biogas. A gas engine burns the biogas and converts its energy (LHV) into electricity (40 %), heat in the flue gas cooled from 450 to 150 °C (22 %) and heat in the engine cooling water from 90 to 40 °C (25 %). The optimisation sets its use between zero and the whole biogas production.
